A sourdough starter is flour and water left to ferment until wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria settle in. Feed it equal weights of flour and water every day at room temperature. After a week it should double within six hours of a feed and smell pleasantly sour, like yoghurt. A rye flour feed speeds things up because rye carries more wild yeast. Keep it in the fridge between bakes and give it two warm feeds before using it to leaven a loaf. See [[Bulk fermentation]] for what happens after mixing.
